clue.text: Better take a leisurely walk in Greece

indicators.note: the stroll is placed inside the abbreviation for the country, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greece
to amble is to walk at a slow relaxed pace

explanation.surface: A punter goes for a gentle stroll while on holiday in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective meaning superior, but it is the noun: one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who places a bet is a punter, one who wagers money.

clue.text: Marx used to grumble over nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits above the other, so 'over' places the grumble first

parts.note: to grouch is to grumble
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Karl Marx was given to grumbling about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marx' points to Karl, but it is Groucho, the comedian of the Marx Brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was the wisecracking moustached comedian among the Marx Brothers film team.

clue.text: No minor member of the previous administration

definitions.meaning: the opposite of minor, greater or more important
John ..., UK prime minister from 1990 to 1997, the government before the one current when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: Not a child, but a senior figure in the last government.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite of minor means greater or important; John Major was the Conservative prime minister before Tony Blair's government.

clue.text: In Honolulu crewman carry cash

indicators.note: the words carry the answer within them, which signals a run of letters concealed inside

explanation.surface: Sailors in Honolulu are carrying money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially gained dishonestly, as in 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Intend to get into torn clothing

indicators.note: the intention word is placed inside the torn word, so 'to get into' marks a container

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn
to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Planning to squeeze into ragged garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: To track round Virginia requires great effort

indicators.note: the track phrase goes round the state's abbreviation, so 'round' marks a container

parts.note: to trail someone is to track or follow them
VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: Following a trail all round the state of Virginia is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful toil, labour involving great exertion.

clue.text: Negotiated to be given medication

definitions.meaning: bargained or discussed terms, as in 'treat with the enemy'

explanation.surface: A patient who bargained to be given drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties treated with each other when they negotiated; a patient treated by a doctor has received medical care.

clue.text: Instrument of agreement, upsetting no-one

parts.note: accord means agreement

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns a piece upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: split as no and one; one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A treaty signed without offending anybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns NOI (no plus I for one) into ION. 'Instrument of agreement' suggests a treaty document.
explanation.definitionFit: An accordion is a bellows-driven musical instrument with keys or buttons.

clue.text: US soldiers take time to support a game defender

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldiers piece is written below the game, holding it up

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
GIs are American soldiers; the plural gives GIS

explanation.surface: American troops pause to back a defender in a sporting match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' wraps the US soldiers round T; 'to support' puts that below the game in this down clue. 'defender' suggests a football player, not one who argues a case.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in support of a cause or belief, defending it.

clue.text: A heavyweight not short on style

parts.note: the opposite of short is long
ton means fashion or style, as in 'the ton' of high society

explanation.surface: A boxer who is far from short and full of style.
explanation.definitionFit: A long ton is the imperial ton of 2,240 pounds, a heavy weight.

clue.text: Aim to be impartial

definitions.meaning: a goal or target to work towards

explanation.surface: Aiming to be fair and even-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective is a goal or target; as an adjective it means unbiased, free of personal feeling.

clue.text: Uneasy lies the head that wears a (Henry IV)

definitions.text: Uneasy lies the head that wears a (Henry IV)

parts.words: Uneasy lies the head that wears a (Henry IV)
parts.note: a famous line from Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2 with its last word missing; the missing word is the royal headgear

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with its final word left for the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The full line is about a king's burden, symbolised by the monarch's headpiece of gold.

clue.text: Get back into the centre of the train

indicators.note: the reversed word is put inside the word for centre, so 'into' marks a container

parts.note: the core is the centre of something

indicators.note: the word get is read backwards, as 'back' asks

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb back aboard into the middle carriage of a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the given word around before 'into' places it inside the centre word; 'train' suggests a railway, not a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a funeral procession, a slow train of mourners following the hearse.

clue.text: Really weary solicitor full of fury

indicators.note: the word for anger sits inside the word for solicitor, so 'full of' marks a container

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, so a tout is one who solicits
ire is anger or fury

explanation.surface: A lawyer in a rage, utterly worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is one who solicits business: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust someone completely is to make them really weary, a phrasal verb of fatigue.

clue.text: Bound to replace bloated GI

indicators.note: re-place means to put the letters in new places, signalling an anagram

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An overweight American soldier is obliged to be replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound in the sense of compelled or duty-bound, under an obligation.

clue.text: Farm manager must bring a toff down to earth

indicators.note: in a down clue the toff piece is brought below the earth piece

parts.note: land is earth or ground
a gent, short for gentleman, is a toff, British slang for a posh person

explanation.surface: The estate manager has to humble a snob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring down to earth' reads as the idiom for humbling someone, but in this down clue it sets the toff below the earth word.
explanation.definitionFit: A land agent manages a country estate or farmland on behalf of its owner.

clue.text: Enraged at being mauled by a hound

indicators.note: something mauled is torn about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Furious at being savaged by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant breed of dog, a type of hound.

clue.text: One large cat from Troy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A single big cat is brought from the ancient city of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilion is the Greek name for the city of Troy, as in the title of Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Coppers put enclosure in front of church

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Police officers build a fence before the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police; here it means copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper coins of low value, such as pennies, are known as coppers.

clue.text: Patrick Moore loses heart to English poet

parts.note: Pat is short for Patrick

indicators.note: the middle letter is dropped, the heart of the surname

explanation.surface: The astronomer Patrick Moore gives way to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Patrick Moore was a well-known British TV astronomer; MOORE loses its central O.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry Patmore was a Victorian poet, author of The Angel in the House.

clue.text: Further comments made by chiropodists?

definitions.meaning: extra remarks printed at the bottom of a page
foot doctors whimsically writing remarks about feet

explanation.surface: Extra remarks offered by foot specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes printed at the bottom of a page give additional remarks on the text; chiropodists, who treat feet, might jot notes about them.

clue.text: A king in banquet, from China, maybe

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the banquet word, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: a feast is a banquet
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch at a feast held in China.
explanation.definitionFit: China is one example of the countries of East Asia.

clue.text: So nylon is manufactured by sole male heir

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up anew, so the letters are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Nylon is made by the only boy in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A family's one boy child would be its single male heir.

clue.text: Severe hesitation to reveal the breastbone

parts.note: stern means severe
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A doctor's hesitant, grave manner in examining the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the flat bone at the front of the chest, anatomical name for the breastbone.

clue.text: Feature otherwise displayed by Judas

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing feature
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or you'll miss it'

explanation.surface: A characteristic shown in another way by the disciple Judas.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name is a byword for a betrayer.

clue.text: It gives light instrument a lining of mesh

indicators.note: the mesh word lines the inside of the instrument word, so this phrase marks a container

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument
net is a mesh fabric

explanation.surface: A light instrument, perhaps a lamp, has a mesh lining.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a crescent-shaped or half-moon window admitting light into a room.

clue.text: Annoys informers

definitions.meaning: people who give information to the police

explanation.surface: Irritates the police spies.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark is British slang for to irritate; narks are also police informers.

clue.text: He attempts to get right into row

indicators.note: the right abbreviation is placed inside the row word, so this marks a container
this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: A man tries to slip into a row.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tries something is a trier, someone making an effort.

clue.text: Old Mrs Merrilies gets a letter from Athens

parts.note: Meg Merrilies is the gypsy woman in Scott's novel Guy Mannering and a poem by Keats

explanation.surface: Old Mrs Merrilies receives a letter posted from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Firm statement that treason is corrupt

indicators.note: to corrupt is to spoil or twist, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forceful claim that treachery is a corrupt act.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident, forceful declaration of belief or fact.

clue.text: Enforce law if a street is in disrepair

indicators.note: something in disrepair is broken, so these letters are to be rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Council officials must apply the law when a road is crumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: In old English law to estreat was to extract a forfeited recognizance from court records for prosecution, enforcing a fine or bail.

clue.text: Remedy for a broken banjo?

definitions.meaning: a broken banjo cannot be strummed, so the phrase splits as a statement about strumming being impossible

explanation.surface: Searching for a cure for a damaged banjo.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet cure; split into two words it says the instrument cannot be played with a sweep of the fingers.
